name: DFW 2001 to 2011 one-story under the 2000 IECC
description: First statewide-code housing: Texas adopted the 2000 IECC in 2001 and kept it through 2011. One story, slab, vented attic, low-e double-pane vinyl windows, R-6 attic flex. No blower-door or duct test was required, so leakage values are estimates. Inspect and override.

sources.citation: RhoeFlow plan v2, Era-based defaults for DFW table (claude/01-plan/research-and-plan.md); estimates to seed the questionnaire
Texas SECO, single-family energy code history: 2000 IECC 2001 to 2011
DOE Building Energy Codes Program, Texas adoption status

ceiling_insulation_cavity_r.basis: Low end of the 2000 to 2015 bucket; R-30 blown was the common minimum under the 2000 IECC. Replace with the measured depth.

window_ufactor.basis: Low-e double-pane vinyl; upper end of the plan range for the early part of the bucket. An NFRC sticker replaces this.

window_shgc.basis: Low-e glazing; midpoint of the plan range.

air_leakage.basis: Upper end of the plan range: the 2000 IECC required no blower-door test. A test result replaces this.

duct_leakage_to_outside.basis: Plan table gives 8 to 12 cfm25 per 100 ft2 for this bucket, read as total to outside. This rate needs the served floor area to become a CFM25 value, which is a WO-02 derivation; the applier records it as skipped until then.
